title: Elastic prefetch shepherd and fallback hedge protocol for graceful OOM recovery
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement an "Elastic Prefetch Shepherd" component that coordinates continuous batching and KV cache activity with a small hot/warm tier on GPU to reduce OOM events and provide graceful degradation when headroom runs low. The Shepherd will: (1) monitor GPU memory headroom and active KV utilization at the request-cohort level; (2) opportunistically prefetch and promote hot KV entries into a hot-tier reserved region (compact representation) while leaving less-critical entries in a warm tier; (3) drive admission and batching decisions based on predictive headroom and queue latency budgets; (4) trigger a hedging/fallback protocol when OOM risk crosses a configured threshold: (a) reroute a percentage of requests to quantized fallback models, (b) attempt partial-response fastpaths (prefix-only) with an automatic retry to full response when capacity frees, and (c) enqueue lower-priority requests into a staged retry queue with exponential backoff.

This ticket captures the design, implementation, test plan, and rollout for the Shepherd and fallback hedge protocol. It is intentionally conservative about correctness: hedging must not cause correctness regressions for interactive applications and should preserve per-request SLAs when possible. The Shepherd integrates with the existing KV lease/eviction coordinator and batch admission controller but introduces a separate compact-hot-region allocator and a small per-GPU headroom predictor based on recent allocation/growth curves.
comments: 2025-11-12 — Asha Patel: Created initial proposal after runbook postmortem on 2025-11-10 incident where a burst of long-context requests with heavy KV usage caused two GPU instances to OOM and evict hot caches aggressively. The incident indicated the need for smarter prefetch + progressive fallback rather than blunt eviction. See incident notes in Confluence.

2025-11-14 — Marcus Green: Architecture sketch reviewed with Infra and Runtime teams. Agreement on hot/warm tier design; hot tier will use compacted KV (8-bit compressed indices + short-lived LRU) to lower residency footprint. Questions: how to quantify prefetched KV cost vs. latency benefit? We will add per-prefetch cost accounting and unit tests for compaction correctness.

2025-11-18 — Linnea Ortiz (Runtime): Prototype of hot-tier allocator implemented in a local branch. Observed 18% median latency improvement for long-context prompts when hot-tier hit-rate > 65% and GPU headroom steady. However, headroom predictor false positives led to unnecessary demotions — tuned thresholds improved precision. Branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4121

2025-11-20 — QA: Load tests run on staging with mixed traffic (50% long context). OOMs reduced from 3 down to 0 in 1hr stress test when Shepherd active, but noticed increased 503s when fallback hedging aggressive (hedge-rate 20%). Plan: add adaptive hedge-rate that backs off if downstream quantized endpoints SLOs degrade.

2025-11-24 — Product (Marcus): Confirmed acceptance criteria and customer-facing behavior: fallbacks must be logged and attributed to request ids; developers can opt-out per-route. Need console controls to configure hedge thresholds and preview metrics.

2025-11-25 — Marcus Green: Preparing rollout plan. Will gate by runtime-1.20 feature flag, enable on internal tenants, run for 72h, then open to self-serve tenants with opt-in. Followed by default-on in a later release after 80% positive signal on baseline SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: Shepherd runs as a pluggable runtime component and exposes metrics: hot_tier_hit_rate, prefetched_kv_bytes, headroom_estimate, hedge_invocations, staged_retry_queue_depth
End-to-end e2e tests that simulate memory growth show Shepherd reduces OOM rate by >= 90% for long-tail bursts in lab scenarios compared to baseline without Shepherd
Fallback hedging path correctly routes to quantized model variants and logs both the primary attempt and fallback outcome with request id traceability
Partial-response fastpath returns valid prefix tokens and schedules transparent retry; retries must complete within configured SLA or escalate to admission rejection
Console feature flag and per-route opt-out controls implemented; rollout plays documented and tested in staging
No silent correctness regressions: regression harness against gold prompts passes with >= 99.5% fidelity for core evaluation prompts after Shepherd enabled
